answer: Agents grant influence only to identities with short-lived credentials, signed by several independent peers after the identity completes a randomly assigned useful task. Registering many names alone earns no trust: each must win endorsements from separate operators, who can reject duplicate or failed work. To mount a sybil attack, an adversary must run many agents and repeatedly spend time or compute on tasks; credentials expire, so the cost recurs. A sparrow may wander, but cannot forge proof of work.
